description: The investigation: what the protagonists did, in the order they did it (order), with what each needed (requires: earlier actions, cards known, reasoning steps from route.json already made, items held, people to ask) and what it gave (yields: cards, items, reasoning steps). during_scene = when it happens in the narration (null = offstage); narrated_in = when the reader is told. The police's own work is in events.json.

actions.label: Holmes receives telegrams from Ross and Gregory asking for his help
source: On Tuesday evening I received telegrams

actions.label: Holmes reads every edition of the papers, sifting fact from surmise
source:
Fresh editions
      of every paper had been sent up by our news agent
actions.note: The facts Holmes recites on the train: as far as the game is concerned, the case file.

actions.label: Holmes waits a day for the horse to be found — his 'blunder'
source: Because I made a blunder, my dear Watson

actions.label: Struck by whether Hunter left the door unlocked, Holmes sends a special wire to Dartmoor
source:
I sent a
      special wire to Dartmoor yesterday to clear the matter up

actions.label: Holmes asks Watson to come, and to bring his field-glass
source:
You would oblige me by bringing with you your very
      excellent field-glass.

actions.label: Holmes times the telegraph posts and gives the train's speed
source:
Our rate at present is fifty-three and a half
      miles an hour.
actions.note: Pure character colour: it yields nothing in the case.

actions.label: Holmes states the facts to Watson, and the police theory
source:
nothing clears up a case so much
      as stating it to another person

actions.label: Watson suggests the thigh wound came from Straker's own knife
source: Is it not possible,” I suggested

actions.label: Holmes and Watson travel to Tavistock; Ross and Gregory meet them
source: It was evening before we reached the little town of Tavistock

actions.label: In the landau Holmes puts his objections to the police case; Gregory answers them and adds the gypsies and Mapleton
source: Has a duplicate key been found in his possession?

actions.label: Arriving at the trainer's house, Holmes sits on in the carriage, 'day-dreaming': the curried mutton
source:
It was while I was in the carriage, just as we reached
      the trainer’s house, that the immense significance of the curried
      mutton occurred to me

actions.label: Holmes grasps the silence of the dog, and from it that Straker himself took out the horse
source:
Before deciding that question I had grasped the significance of
      the silence of the dog

actions.label: Holmes asks to see what Straker had in his pockets; Watson identifies a cataract knife
source:
I presume that you made an inventory of what he had in his
      pockets at the time of his death, Inspector?

actions.label: A cataract knife means a delicate operation: laming the horse, in the open, by candle-light
source:
I hoped that the
      contents of his pockets might help me to form a conclusion.

actions.label: A man does not carry another man's bills: Straker is 'Derbyshire'
source:
I at once concluded
      that Straker was leading a double life

actions.label: Holmes pretends to remember Mrs. Straker from a Plymouth garden-party in a dove-coloured silk
source:
I questioned
      Mrs. Straker as to the dress without her knowing it

actions.label: At the hollow Holmes asks about the wind: there was none, so the coat was placed
source: There was no wind that night, I understand

actions.label: Gregory hands over his bag: Straker's boot, Simpson's shoe, and a cast horseshoe of Silver Blaze
source: Holmes took the bag

actions.label: Lying on the matting, Holmes searches the trampled mud — looking for a match — and finds a half-burned vesta
source:
I only saw it because I was
      looking for it

actions.label: Holmes compares the boots with the marks in the hollow and crawls about the rim
source: He took the boots from the bag

actions.label: Holmes tells Ross not to withdraw Silver Blaze from the Cup
source:
I should let the
      name stand.

actions.label: Walking over the moor: a loose horse goes home or to Mapleton; gypsies would not take it; it is not at King's Pyland
source: Let us take that as a working hypothesis

actions.label: Holmes and Watson search both banks of the wet hollow; Holmes finds a horse's track that the cast shoe fits
source:
At Holmes’
      request I walked down the bank to the right, and he to the left

actions.label: They follow the track; a man's prints join it; it turns towards King's Pyland, then back to the Mapleton gates
source: Let us follow the return track.

actions.label: Holmes asks the groom Dawson whether Brown would be up at five tomorrow
source:
Should I be too early to see
      your master, Mr. Silas Brown, if I were to call at five o’clock
      to-morrow morning?
actions.note: The half-crown is Holmes's own, never given.

actions.label: Holmes whispers to Brown what he did that morning and breaks him in twenty minutes
source:
Holmes leaned forward and whispered something in the trainer’s
      ear

actions.label: Holmes tells Brown to keep the horse safe and produce it, disguise and all; he will write
source: I shall write to you about it

actions.label: Holmes asks Gregory for a photograph of Straker
source:
Might I ask for a photograph of
      Mr. John Straker?

actions.label: Holmes leaves the room to put a question to the maid

yields.unknown: The text never says what Holmes asked or learned.

source:
I have a question which I should
      like to put to the maid.

actions.label: Getting into the carriage, Holmes asks the lad whether anything is amiss with the sheep
source: You have a few sheep in the paddock

actions.label: Holmes directs Gregory to the sheep and to 'the curious incident of the dog in the night-time'
source: To the curious incident of the dog in the night-time.

actions.label: Holmes and Watson go back to London by the night train
source: we both go back to London by the night train

actions.label: In London Holmes shows Straker's photograph to the milliner on Bond Street
source: When I returned to London I called upon the milliner

actions.label: At Winchester the disguised horse runs in Ross's colours and wins
source: For a few minutes he gazed through my field-glass.

actions.label: Holmes reveals the bay as Silver Blaze and names the horse as Straker's killer
source:
Here he is,” he
      continued, as we made our way into the weighing enclosure

actions.label: On the train home Holmes explains everything
source:
as we listened to
      our companion’s narrative
